audit_summary: All five facts are directly supported by the cited repository files and line ranges.

facts.statement: The pylint package publicly exports modify_sys_path via __all__.
The module-execution entry point imports pylint, calls pylint.modify_sys_path(), and then calls pylint.run_pylint().
modify_sys_path documents that it strips the current working directory and states that the first entry will always be either an empty string or the working directory.
The first operation in modify_sys_path is an unconditional sys.path.pop(0); cwd and PYTHONPATH are examined only afterward.
The existing modify_sys_path test cases initialize sys.path with either the mocked cwd or an empty string as the first entry and assert that this entry is removed.

scope_summary: At base commit 684a1d6aa0a6791e20078bc524f97c8906332390, Pylint’s module entry point calls modify_sys_path(), whose first operation unconditionally removes sys.path[0]. Existing tests cover first entries equal to the mocked working directory or an empty string, but not an unrelated path inserted at index 0.
unknowns: The repository does not establish intended behavior when sys.path is empty or when its first entry is an unrelated path such as one injected by a bundling extension.
The repository does not contain a test invoking pylint through runpy.run_module.
